headline: Seven majors above their 200-day, but MACD hasn't confirmed a single one
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's unusually clean today: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and BNB are all above their 200-day lines with golden crosses in place, while DOGE and ADA sit below theirs. That's five majors in a confirmed uptrend structure and two laggards still working through repair. Bitcoin at $77,795.39 is up 1.6% on the day, essentially flat on the week (+0.5%), but up 20.2% on the month, a reminder that the daily print and the trend can tell different stories without contradicting each other. ETH is the standout, up 5.6% on the day, 6.5% on the week, and 34.2% on the month, with RSI at 66.4, the hottest reading on the board.

Here's the divergence worth naming: not one of these seven assets shows MACD above its signal line, despite five of them trending above their 200-day average with RSI readings in the 51 to 66 range (comfortably below overbought territory north of 70). That's a market grinding higher on trend and breadth without fresh momentum confirmation underneath it. It's not a warning light, it's a texture: the move up has been steady rather than accelerating, and MACD is telling you the short-term thrust has cooled even as price keeps climbing. Worth watching whether that gap closes with MACD catching up, or with price rolling over to meet it.

Positioning adds a layer. BTC funding on OKX sits at 0.0059% per 8 hours (6.4% annualized), modest by crypto standards, with open interest at $2.14B and a long/short ratio of 1.51, meaning longs outnumber shorts by half again. ETH funding is a touch richer at 7.4% annualized with OI of $1.65B, but its long/short ratio is closer to balanced at 1.10. The real crowding shows up further out on the risk curve: DOGE funding is running hot at 10.5% annualized with a long/short ratio of 4.29, and SOL's ratio is 2.12 despite funding of just 0.6% annualized, an odd pairing of heavy long-side lean with cheap cost to hold it. Liquidations over the last hour lean long-side across BTC ($381,956 longs vs $150,045 shorts) and SOL ($610,014 longs vs $23,118 shorts), consistent with a market where longs have been the crowded, exposed trade even as prices grind up.

The flows disagree with each other in a way that matters. BTC spot ETFs saw an outflow of $282.7M on 10 Sep 2026, yet the five-session net is a $455.9M inflow, with only 3 same-direction days, so this is a choppy tape, not a clean trend in either direction. ETH ETFs show the identical pattern: a $29.9M outflow on the day against a $147.8M five-session inflow, with just 1 same-direction day. Meanwhile whale wallets moved $38.4M net onto exchanges over the last 24 hours, mostly a $89.6M inflow to Coinbase Institutional partially offset by a $51.2M outflow from the same venue. Zooming out to the weekly whale series: onto-exchange moves of $944M (week ending Aug 21) and $857M (week ending Aug 28), then a reversal to $432M off exchanges (week ending Sep 04), then back onto exchanges at $572M (week ending Sep 11). That's not a steady drift either way, it's a market moving coin around in both directions depending on the week. Stablecoin float, the market's dry powder, sits at $310.0B, up 1.28% over 30 days, a slow build rather than a surge.

Sentiment sits at 56, Greed, inside its own 30-day range of 29 to 74, so the crowd is warm but not at an extreme. That's roughly in line with what the tape shows: real uptrend structure, but without the overheated RSI or aggressive MACD confirmation that would mark euphoria. The disagreement worth watching isn't sentiment versus price today, it's the MACD-versus-trend gap and the choppy ETF and whale windows. Things to watch from here: whether MACD crosses above signal on BTC or ETH to confirm the move, whether the weekly whale series produces back-to-back off-exchange weeks, and whether BTC ETF flows string together same-direction days rather than alternating outflow-then-inflow prints.
